assessmentProtocols.materials: Inclusive fictional family cards plus voluntary non-sensitive descriptions of ordinary celebrations/practices from the learner and a peer; an educator may provide anonymized peer-approved information. Include varied family structures without ranking them.
assessmentProtocols.task: Describe how each family is structured and compare one similarity/difference in its practices with the peer’s; identify that different families remain families. No disclosure about religion, care status or private relationships is compelled.
assessmentProtocols.success: Accurate inclusive family descriptions and a supported own/peer comparison rather than treating the learner’s family as the universal model.
assessmentProtocols.nearMiss: Labels a different family as not a real family, or only names an event without a comparison.
assessmentProtocols.boundary: Source-fit authoring design, not evidence of a learner pass; source examples are illustrative rather than an exhaustive required family-type checklist.

assessmentProtocols.materials: A voluntary non-sensitive family or actual school/community tradition and a dated past/present resource prepared by an adult. The source may be supplied; no home address or sensitive family history is needed.
assessmentProtocols.task: Ask questions whose answers could show what the tradition was like before and now and what changed or continued. Explain which question would help investigate the chosen own-community tradition.
assessmentProtocols.success: Questions guide the actual past/present tradition investigation, not just name an object or ask an unrelated fact.
assessmentProtocols.nearMiss: Asks only an unrelated preference question or assumes the reason for change without investigation.
assessmentProtocols.boundary: This resolves question formulation, not the later evaluation/conclusion requirements of the whole inquiry.

assessmentProtocols.materials: Dated/ordered voluntary family records or supplied authentic own-community events spanning multiple generations. Use non-sensitive community records if personal family history is unsuitable.
assessmentProtocols.task: Place events/people in an unscaled sequence, explain before/after relationships and add an event using source information.
assessmentProtocols.success: Correctly sequences the multi-generation events and justifies an added event with the supplied record.
assessmentProtocols.nearMiss: Groups events by liking or makes equal timeline spacing mean equal duration despite no scale.
assessmentProtocols.boundary: A source-fit task specification; no actual learner records are requested to certify authoring coverage.

assessmentProtocols.materials: A globe and at least two differently centred/oriented world maps, stated seven-continent convention, familiar location markers and an adult-verified geographical reference key. The independent task does not merely copy complete printed labels.
task: Name/locate the seven continents in the specified model and distinguish continent/country/ocean references. Explain that Oceania is a region rather than a continent under the stated NationalGeographic model, without declaring every other map convention false.
Name/locate significant waters through the existing FiveOceans claim and recognize their connected global water body.

Identify geographic poles and Equator, then Northern/Southern Hemispheres; classify provided points and a region crossing the Equator. No mandatory PrimeMeridian/Eastern/Western inventory is inferred from the Ontario clause.

Transfer to another map/globe view without using physical page-up as geographic north. A map projection can distort or omit a pole; use the globe/reference when the representation does not establish it.
assessmentProtocols.positive: Correctly identifies the required continent/water/reference features and transfers across views, keeping geographic conventions explicit.
assessmentProtocols.nearMiss: Names Canada as a continent, treats Equator as a country border, changes hemispheres when the globe is turned, or copies labels without retaining locations.
assessmentProtocols.transfer: Differently centred map and turned globe, with a crossing region and a supplied alternative grouping convention.
assessmentProtocols.boundary: This accounts for source identification, not every climate mechanism, country fact or map operation. The pole topic’s corrected coldness explanation remains in its own complete assessment; it is not invented as an additional mandatory B3.2 clause.

assessmentProtocols.task: Use the attributed cases to identify what knowledge/practice is shared, who shares/learns it and how the community activity or surviving source lets later people learn. Compare oral conversations, written records and community teaching/gatherings; describe the actual channel rather than just name a holiday/food.
assessmentProtocols.positive: Identifies multiple concrete ways cultural/community knowledge is passed through the provided practices, with correct source/people attribution.
assessmentProtocols.nearMiss: Only names a food, language or event with no account of how people learn/share it, or generalizes one case to all peoples.
assessmentProtocols.transfer: Another ordinary source-supported community practice with a different channel, identifying what is preserved/shared rather than copying a phrase.

assessmentProtocols.task: Describe the relevant family practice and identify who shares what with another generation and how the shared celebration/practice carries it. Compare the family conversation/gathering channel with another family practice, retaining the actual FNMI case rather than replacing it with a generic family story.
assessmentProtocols.positive: Identifies several concrete family sharing/learning practices, including the specific Métis family account, without assuming cultural membership from ancestry or participation alone.
assessmentProtocols.nearMiss: Only names relatives or a celebration; omits the sharing/learning channel or the required attributed FNMI family practice.
assessmentProtocols.transfer: A different family practice/account while keeping its people, evidence and channel distinct.
